name: Chloe Bennett
presenting_complaint: Bloody diarrhoea up to 10 times a day for a week with cramping and fever

medical_history.social: University student. Non-smoker. Minimal alcohol. Recently stopped mesalazine for 2 weeks due to cost. No recent travel or antibiotics.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: A 27-year-old woman with known ulcerative colitis presents with 1 week of worsening bloody diarrhoea up to 10 times per day, crampy abdominal pain, urgency and fever. She stopped her mesalazine 2 weeks ago. She looks unwell and dehydrated. Obs: BP 108/68, HR 112, RR 18, temp 38.1, SpO2 98% on room air. Abdomen is diffusely tender but soft with no rebound.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: Flare characterisation: stool frequency (up to 10/day), amount of blood, nocturnal symptoms, urgency, tenesmus, duration 1 week
Severity markers for Truelove & Witts: fever, tachycardia, and screen for symptoms of anaemia
Precipitants: mesalazine non-adherence (stopped 2 weeks ago), recent NSAIDs, antibiotics, or infective contacts/travel
Systemic and extra-intestinal features: weight loss, arthralgia, eye/skin symptoms, mouth ulcers
Red-flag screen for toxic megacolon/perforation: severe distension, worsening pain, reduced stool output with rising fever, systemic toxicity
Medication and allergy history; VTE risk factors; last menstrual period / pregnancy status
objective: Grade severity using Truelove & Witts criteria (>6 bloody stools/day plus fever, tachycardia >90, anaemia, raised ESR/CRP = severe)
Abdominal examination: distension, tenderness, guarding/rebound (peritonism), bowel sounds — assess for toxic megacolon
Stool chart commenced; stool sample for MC&S AND Clostridioides difficile toxin to exclude infection
Bloods: FBC (anaemia, WCC), UEC + electrolytes (hypokalaemia), CRP/ESR, LFTs, albumin, iron studies, group and hold, blood cultures if febrile
Abdominal X-ray (erect/supine) to assess colonic diameter and exclude toxic megacolon/perforation; repeat daily if unwell
Vital signs monitoring and fluid balance chart; document hydration status
assessment: Acute severe ulcerative colitis flare (Truelove & Witts severe) precipitated by mesalazine non-adherence
Exclude superimposed infection — C. difficile and enteric pathogens — before attributing solely to flare
Assess for and actively exclude toxic megacolon and perforation (surgical emergencies)
Consider CMV colitis if refractory to steroids
plan: VTE prophylaxis with prophylactic LMWH (e.g. enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily) DESPITE rectal bleeding — flares are strongly prothrombotic
IV corticosteroids: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV QID (or methylprednisolone 60 mg IV daily)
IV fluid resuscitation and correct electrolytes, especially potassium (hypokalaemia predisposes to toxic megacolon)
Send stool MC&S and C. difficile toxin; commence stool frequency/blood chart; withhold antibiotics unless infection or perforation suspected
Do NOT prescribe antimotility agents (loperamide/opioids/anticholinergics) — they can precipitate toxic megacolon
Daily abdominal examination, inflammatory markers and abdominal X-ray to monitor colonic diameter for toxic megacolon
Early gastroenterology referral AND surgical review; plan day-3 assessment for rescue therapy (infliximab/ciclosporin) vs colectomy in non-responders
Nutritional assessment, thromboprophylaxis review, VTE education, and continue iron replacement; nil aggravating medications

critical_errors: Prescribing antimotility agents (loperamide, opioids or anticholinergics) which risk precipitating toxic megacolon
Withholding VTE prophylaxis because the patient is having bloody diarrhoea — prophylaxis is still required in an acute flare
Failing to recognise or monitor for toxic megacolon/perforation (no abdominal X-ray, no surgical involvement)
Not sending stool for MC&S and C. difficile toxin, missing superimposed infection before escalating immunosuppression
must_not_miss: Toxic megacolon (monitored with serial abdominal X-ray and examination; surgical review arranged)
Superimposed infection excluded (stool MC&S and C. difficile toxin)
Acute severe colitis graded (Truelove & Witts) and IV corticosteroids commenced
